Volkswagen is getting ready to launch a new electric car starting at about €20,000 ($22,000) in 2027, and it looks like the entry-level EV may no longer be nameless. A newly filed trademark could have just given away what VW plans to call it.
Volkswagen trademarks ID. UP as potential entry-level EV
The new entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said last March after unveiling the ID. EVERY1 concept car.
Volkswagen said the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).
The new model will sit below the ID. Polo in Volkswagen’s Electric Urban Car Family, a lineup of compact, affordable electric cars.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Volkswagen’s current entry-level EV lineup includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, the Cupra Raval, and Skoda Epiq, all based on its new MEB+ platform.
After launching the lower-priced standard versions of the ID. Polo and ID. Cross recently, starting at €24,995 and €27,995, respectively, Volkswagen is preparing to launch an even smaller, more affordable EV next year.
A recent trademark filing with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the German DPMA may have just revealed the name of VW’s upcoming €20,000 EV.
Volkswagen trademark application for the name ID. UP (Source: EUIPO)
Volkswagen filed a trademark application for the name ID. UP on October 22, 2026, with the EUIPO and DPMA, suggesting this will be the name of the upcoming electric car in 2027.
The trademark follows previous reports that VW planned to revive the former Up! name as part of its shift away from its previous numerical naming scheme (ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, etc.).
Volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.
VW Brand CEO Thomas Schäfer introduces the ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
The VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.
Volkswagen said it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).
The production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine new models VW plans to launch by 2027.
Volkswagen ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen previously said the entry-level EV will be 3,880 mm long, which would position it between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and the ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.
The VW Group’s new Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.
All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.
Volkswagen ID. EVERY1 concept car interior (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen said the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal, software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which it is developing through its joint venture with Rivian.
In March, the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies (RV Tech) joint venture tested the new SDV architecture on the ID. EVERY1, alongside Audi and Scout reference vehicles, validating over-the-air (OTA) capabilities.
The new architecture will enable “highly automated driving features” and “advanced infotainment solutions,” with continuous OTA updates.
While VW said it will deploy the SDV architecture in “electric vehicles across markets in the Western Hemisphere,” the entry-level EV is not expected to reach the States.
Volkswagen is, however, preparing to launch the ID. Tiguan , which will launch in 2027 as the successor to the ID.4 (and ID.5 in Europe).

Cubert Is a Pop-Top VW Caddy Micro-Camper With an Incredibly Homey Interior
13 photos
Photo: Bodans
When it comes to Volkswagen vehicles that can be turned into campers, the Caddy may not be the first model that comes to mind. The Crafter, the Transporter, and the Multivan are definitely more popular choices, but the Caddy’s compact dimensions make it an interesting alternative for those looking for a more agile, maneuverable, and practical micro-camper.
British converter Bodans has seen the potential of the VW Caddy as a practical base for micro camper conversions and has created the Cubert, a practical compact build with the essential features for camping that proves you don’t necessarily need a large van to enjoy the freedom of the open road.
Based on the Volkswagen Caddy Maxi , which boasts a longer wheelbase and additional interior space compared with the standard Caddy, Bodans’ Cubert is aimed at campers who want a vehicle that can serve as both a daily commuter and a weekend adventure rig.
The Cubert typically starts with a brand-new VW Caddy Maxi Commerce or Plus with the manufacturer’s 114-hp plug-in hybrid drivetrain, offering up to 116 km (72 miles) of range. The unit pictured here measures approximately 485 cm (191 inches) in length and features a simple floor plan that makes great use of the vehicle’s limited floor space and a pop-top roof, which opens up valuable headroom and provides excellent ventilation through the mesh windows.
Photo: Bodans If anything, this smart conversion proves Caddy campers are not just smaller campers but rather belong in a category of their own. They drive like a modern hatchback rather than a heavy motorhome, get great fuel economy, and can easily squeeze into tight country lanes. And besides their practicality for daily use, they represent a step up for people who want more comfort than a tent or a mattress in the back.
Unlike other Caddy conversions that only have basic sleeping arrangements, modular elements, and removable kitchens, the Cubert is a full-fledged conversion with a permanent interior designed like a miniature apartment on wheels. It has a proper kitchen, comfortable seating, integrated storage, and generous headroom thanks to that elevating roof.
For its interior layout, Bodans has taken inspiration from larger camper vans, placing a long, side-facing sofa on one side and a kitchen block along the opposite wall. This leaves a central aisle for easy passage from front to back and between the two areas.
For sleeping, the sofa pulls out into a comfortable bed for two. Underneath it, there is storage for camping equipment and other personal belongings, and a removable Lagun-style table is attached to the side of the sofa for dining or working on the road.
Photo: Bodans The kitchen block is small, but that’s to be expected given the size of the vehicle. However, it’s very practical, with a curved design that facilitates movement inside the camper. It features a roller door that gives access to a shelved cabinet inside and glossy white countertops, which give it a sleek, contemporary look.
It’s also very functional, with an integrated stainless steel sink featuring a collapsible faucet and an electric induction hob, both covered by a glass lid. A two-burner gas alternative is available for buyers who prefer it. There is also a Dometic drawer fridge neatly tucked under the sofa, as well as additional storage in a rear cabinet console behind the sofa. Besides providing more room for storing things and adding another useful worktop surface, this standalone unit incorporates the camper’s electrical controls.
The Reimo rear elevating roof is a standard inclusion, making the interior more livable, open, and comfortable to move around when raised. It comes with mesh windows and can be fitted with an optional double mattress, turning the Cubert into a four-berth camper .
Photo: Bodans Bodans has also paid attention to the aesthetics of the interior living space. While other conversions leave the original automotive trim exposed, the Cubert has received light-gray carpet-style lining on the walls and ceiling, which, combined with gray flooring, upholstered furniture, and integrated LED lights, creates a warmer, more serene ambience than one might expect in a small commercial van conversion.
It’s worth mentioning that the Cubert is not a new conversion offered by Bodans, but it has come to our attention because the outfitter gave it a refresh. The main upgrade is the introduction of an updated electrical system meant to allow for gas-free camping.
Photo: Bodans For campers who want to travel without LPG bottles, the induction hob can operate off the camper's electrical system with 230v mains off-grid power station and a 3,000W Renogy inverter. A slimline 100W roof-mounted solar panel can also be added as an upgrade. The camper also has an onboard fresh-water container, a submersible pump, and a waste outlet.
Along with the rooftop mattress and solar panel, a diesel-powered blown-air heating and a microwave are also included on the list of optional extras. Buyers can also choose from a wide range of colors and interior furnishings to give the interior a more personalized look.
In terms of pricing, the VW Caddy Cubert camper van starts at £49,995 (about $66,150 at current exchange rates) when it is based on a new Caddy van. If you prefer to use a second-hand vehicle, the cost of the conversion lowers to £43,995 ($58,225).

Geologist Ed Walker handles drill core at Torngat Metals’ Strange Lake rare earth project in northern Quebec in August 2023. Credit: Torngat Metals/Business Wire.
By: Noah Chaikin November 13, 2026
A longer trade truce with China could ease manufacturers’ rare earth supply fears while making potential Canadian alternatives harder to finance. On Nov. 9, Beijing extended the suspension of its broader October 2025 restrictions on rare earth exports worldwide until Jan. 10, 2027, matching its trade truce with Washington. Licensing rules introduced in April 2025 remain in force, including those affecting permanent magnets used in electric motors.
Access to established Chinese suppliers gives manufacturers a reason to postpone supply agreements with Canadian mine developers that could require testing new materials and accepting higher prices. Neither Wicheeda nor Strange Lake is producing. Buyers would be committing to future supply, helping developers obtain the financing needed to build their projects.
Government financing commitments for critical minerals reached about $65 billion (C$91.8 billion) in advanced economies in 2025, more than four times their 2023 level, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). Capital spending fell 9% that year among 24 major mining companies tracked by the agency, with battery metals driving the decline. For Canadian rare earth developers, public backing still needs to be matched by customers willing to commit to alternative supply.
Easing Chinese controls could leave committed buyers paying more than competitors who hold off, the University of Sydney’s United States Studies Centre warned in September . The centre linked difficulty securing buyers to years of delay before Arafura Rare Earths’ (ASX: ARU) May 2026 investment decision for its Nolans project in Australia. Arafura requires binding sales agreements covering 80% of planned neodymium and praseodymium production before drawing senior debt, demonstrating why buyer hesitation can hold up financing.
Projects need offtakes
Defense Metals’ (TSXV: DEFN; US-OTC: DFMTF) proposed Wicheeda rare earth project in British Columbia received Export Development Canada’s June 2025 expression of interest in arranging up to $250 million in development and construction loans. Financing remains conditional on the lender’s project review, while a May 2026 supply and investment memorandum with South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean (KRX: 042660) and Hanwha Corp. (KRX: 000880) doesn’t guarantee purchases.
Those discussions need to produce binding sales of mixed rare earth carbonate for further separation, supporting Wicheeda’s target of completing a feasibility study and securing offtake in 2027 before closing financing in 2028.
Torngat Metals signed a 10-year agreement with French processor Carester in October 2025 for its Strange Lake project in northern Quebec, demonstrating that some buyers are already making long-term commitments to diversify. The contract covers a partially separated stream containing dysprosium and terbium for Carester’s Caremag subsidiary.
Torngat is seeking additional buyers for separated oxides from its proposed operation. Up to C$165 million of public lending announced in June 2025 supports preconstruction work, leaving the larger construction financing package to be assembled. Torngat is targeting mine commissioning in 2030, subject to regulatory approvals.
These examples show why customer commitments matter to financing; they do not establish that trade truces have delayed either Canadian project. The risk is that further extensions encourage buyers to postpone contracts or seek shorter terms, weakening the sales commitments available to support construction loans.
Supporting future supply
To sustain investment through further truces, Ottawa should negotiate pooled purchases with allied processors and magnet manufacturers, using capped public support to secure contracts with Canadian suppliers. Combining orders would spread the commitment across creditworthy companies, each responsible for specified quantities at minimum prices over a period that supports debt repayment. Processors would provide the link between Canadian mine output and the oxides magnet manufacturers require. Automakers should help fund those commitments, since tripling rare earth prices would add just 0.1% to a car’s price, according to the IEA.
Japan has already linked public backing with industrial purchases through Japan Australia Rare Earths, a joint venture of its state metals agency and trading house Sojitz (TSE: 2768). Its March 2026 agreement commits to buying 5,000 tonnes of neodymium and praseodymium annually from Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) through 2038 at a $110-per-kg floor. The arrangement gives Lynas predictable sales volumes and a minimum price.
Ottawa should assess whether the Canada Critical Minerals Accelerator could help finance similar purchasing agreements for Canadian rare earths, with allied governments sharing the cost. Its C$2 billion is an announced five-year allocation, with investments approved individually. Competitive bids would set a fixed public payment per unit to Canadian suppliers, payable against verified deliveries within agreed volume and time limits.
For illustration, a contract for a specified rare earth oxide might guarantee the supplier $100 per kg, with governments contributing $20 and the buyer paying $80. If equivalent Chinese material fell to $60 per kg, those obligations would remain unchanged. Public payments would be made only against verified deliveries within the agreed support limits.
Buyers would bear the risk of cheaper competing supply, while developers would remain responsible for construction and delivery.
For deliveries outside the public support limits, buyers would pay the full agreed minimum price, with no further taxpayer contribution.
Price support could lift the internal rate of return of a typical rare earth refinery outside China by about 2.4 percentage points at an average annual public cost of $18 million, according to IEA modelling .
Canada’s mineral future cannot depend on another disruption in Chinese supply. Beijing may extend its suspension again beyond Jan. 10, so Ottawa should use the Nov. 18–19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen, China, to begin negotiations with allies on pooled purchase contracts. Those contracts would help Canadian projects secure construction financing even if relations with China improve.
Noah Chaikin is a strategy consultant in Kearney’s Foresight practice in Toronto, advising executives on geopolitics, critical minerals and economic security. The author has no client relationships with the companies named in this article. The views expressed are his own.

source_document.body:
BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.
BYD opens pre-orders for the third-gen Tang SUV
The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.
We knew it was coming soon after the new model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.
BYD announced on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.
The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).
All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.
Inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.
BYD third-generation Tang electric SUV interior (Source: Lu Tian)
Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.
The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD said.
BYD third-generation Tang electric SUV interior (Source: Lu Tian)
Like many of its new flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.
Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.
Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division said third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.
BYD third-generation Tang EV SUV (Source: Lu Tian)
The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it launched in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.
Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.
The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).
Will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

Mercedes-Benz Freezes All Investments, Considers Shutting Down Plants
8 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
Mercedes-Benz has frozen all new investments at its German facilities and is evaluating potential plant closures. The decision was announced to the staff in an internal memo and escalates a major standoff with labor unions over high domestic manufacturing costs and declining profits.
Chief production officer Michael Schiebe confirmed that the executive board jointly decided to halt all further investments in German sites. Projects that are already underway, such as the billion-euro paint shop at the Sindelfingen plant, will continue as planned, the German media notes.
Schiebe previously warned that one German assembly plant and one powertran plant could shut down if cost-cutting targets are missed. Furthermore, Human Resources board member Britta Seeger explained that, while the company hopes to avoid closures , it is now forced to examine which German sites it can afford to maintain active and which should be shut down.
Amid union talks with the works council and IG Metall trade union stalled, the automaker’s management has already pointed out that without changes to domestic cost structures, production of next-generation vehicle models will move exclusively abroad.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz Management wants workers to increase their standard workweek from 35 to 40 hours per week without a pay raise and accept cuts to special bonuses. In the meantime, the unions are pushing for wage increases, Deutsche Welle reports .
According to internal reports, with results revealed by Michael Schiebe, labor and administrative costs in Germany are up to five times higher than at its plants in Eastern Europe, such as Kecskemet in Hungary, Sebes and Cugir operated through two subsidiaries in Romania, and Jawor in Poland.
The potential move mirrors the general turmoil across Germany’s automotive industry, where auto giant Volkswagen, through Porsche and Audi, along with major suppliers, such as Schaeffler, are executing severe restructuring and job cuts.
Furthermore, demand in China has dropped sharply amid fierce competition from domestic carmakers. China is Mercedes-Benz's largest single-country market, accounting for roughly 30% of its global passenger car sales. While total regional volume in Europe is slightly larger than China alone, China easily outpaces every individual country, including the United States and Germany.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz Whatever move Mercedes-Benz makes in Germany, it will have no negative impact whatsoever on the automaker’s Tuscaloosa plant in Alabama. In March 2026, Mercedes-Benz Group committed to a $4 billion investment through 2030 to upgrade and expand its Vane facility in Tuscaloosa County, which is part of a broader $7 billion U.S. manufacturing push.
The facility will most likely benefit from the brand’s production strategy in Germany. To offset tariffs imposed by the Trump administration, Mercedes is already moving production of its high-volume GLC compact crossover from Germany to the United States.
Assembly is scheduled to kick off in late 2027, pushing the plant's annual output capacity toward 340,000 vehicles. Mercedes-Benz’s U.S. plant currently employs 5,800 workers and exports about 60% of its output. The plant builds luxury SUVs, such as the GLE , GLS, and all-electric EQE and EQS SUVs.

Save This Pontiac: 1967 Car Needs a Complete Restoration, Work Under Way
45 photos
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1
Runs and drives but still needs work. This is the essential information you need to know about this 1967 Pontiac, as the car is here because it needs a new owner willing to pick up from where its restoration work was suspended.
This isn’t the most desirable Pontiac, but it still makes for a fantastic daily driver if you’re in the market for an affordable project.
The restoration work has already started, but the seller didn’t share additional information as to whether they wanted to keep this Pontiac original or go for a custom build that just works.
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1 The Tempest family included multiple choices, including the Custom convertible, the Custom 4-door hardtop, and the Custom Sports Coupe, but Pontiac used every opportunity to brag about its new lineup of wagons.
The GM brand used its marketing papers to highlight the low price of its wagons, despite the impressive lineup of features installed at no extra cost.
“Our new Tempest Safari is unquestionably the most elegant wagon ever to grace the low-price field,” Pontiac said. “We turned our stylists and engineers loose on this one, and they came up with things like walnut wood grain styled panels, thick nylon blend carpeting, and all Morrokide interior, plus a revolutionary overhead cam 6 engine.”
It worked. The Tempest was a successful model, despite not selling in the big numbers that Pontiac hoped and certainly not becoming as desirable as other models, such as the GTO .
It also didn’t get the powerful engines on the GTO, as the focus was on building an affordable model whose focus was also on economy.
The standard choice was a 230 six with only 165 horsepower, while a similar version of this engine but with a higher compression ratio, a four-barrel carburetor, and running on premium fuel increased the output to 215 horsepower.
If you wanted V8 power, the first option was a 326 with 250 horsepower. It sported a two-barrel carburetor. The HO version dropped the two-barrel for a four-barrel and used a dual-exhaust system to produce 285 horsepower. This engine was not available on station wagons, so the highest you could go on a Tempest wagon was the regular version of the 326.
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1 This Tempest still has an engine under the hood, and the good news is that it starts and runs. “It will go into drive and reverse,” the seller explains, but that’s all the good news end. The car needs urgent work, and its stopping power is very limited at this point.
“The fuel tank will hold about a quarter tank but has been patched with fuel tank epoxy over a small pinhole,” the seller notes.
My recommendation is that you go there in person to inspect this Pontiac if you are interested in buying the car, especially if you don’t live far away and the travel costs wouldn’t be too high.
The metal appears to be in decent condition, though the car already sports some patches on the floor. “The frame seems solid,” the owner explains, but you’ll find rust around the trunk. Some bondo repairs have already been made.
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1 This Pontiac Tempest is a solid project, but it’s pretty clear that this car is not supposed to be a collectible or anything similar. It’s an honest restoration candidate, and I doubt that anyone would buy this car to keep it original and turn it into an occasional driver. If anything, it makes more sense as a daily driver, especially considering the V8 under the hood.
The selling price is always the one that makes a huge difference between a vehicle that would stay where it is for much longer or a restoration candidate that eventually receives this long overdue refresh.
Fortunately, this Tempest isn’t at all expensive, and that’s why many people have decided to add it to their watchlists. There are 18 people who decided to keep an eye on this Pontiac, and there’s a good chance more users will save the listing once it gets more exposure.
The owner wants $4,200 for this Pontiac, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay. This means other offers would also be considered, but there’s no guarantee the price would drop significantly. However, I don’t expect any offer below $4,000 to be accepted, but you should be able to discuss all these details on the phone or during your live inspection.
The vehicle is parked in Berea, Kentucky, and considering the engine has seen better days and the stopping power isn’t the best, you should also bring transportation to take the car home. You still have 11 days to figure out if you should buy the car, but you’d better make a decision as fast as possible because someone else might trigger the BIN option at any moment.
A clean title is also available for the buyer, but no other papers are offered.

Private Collector Sells 1958 Chevrolet Impala That Still Wears the Original Paint, Rebuilt V8
7 photos
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1
1958 was the year for the Impala, and this specimen is here to remind the world why. The car, which is being sold by a private collector who listed it on eBay, has already received essential work, including a rebuilt engine. It’s not a spotless Impala, so whoever buys it needs to continue the work to achieve the spotless full-size Chevy so many people are dreaming about.
The car still wears the original paint, and this is fantastic news for someone who loves the classic 1958 Impala design.
It doesn’t have the best 1958 engine, but the unit under the hood has already been rebuilt, so if you want to hop in and drive, you should be able to do that without spending more dollars.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The 1957 Bel Air paved the road for an obvious Chevrolet comeback in the American car space. With the Impala presented in 1956 as a concept at GM’s motor show, it was only a matter of time until the American carmaker graduated it from the drawing board to the assembly lines.
It turns out that two years were enough, as the Impala saw daylight as a production-ready model in 1958. It wasn’t a stand-alone series but a Bel Air version - the top version, to be more precise - and it could be ordered as a hardtop and a convertible.
The Impala was the model that propelled Chevrolet to the leading spot in the United States, helping the carmaker reach sales of 1.25 million cars. Ford was the runner-up with 1.03 million cars.
The Impala wasn’t necessarily an affordable car, but it still sold like hotcakes. The hardtop started at $2,586, while the convertible carried a base price of $2,724.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 In addition to the Impala, the big news in 1958 was the introduction of the 348 big-block unit. This engine marked Chevrolet’s foray into the big-block world, joining the lineup with multiple configurations. The top was the M-coded Special Turbo-Thrust with an 11:1 compression ratio and solid lifters. It was an expensive engine, but it developed 315 horsepower.
It was highly desirable that year, and it is still highly desirable today. In terms of small-block power, the top configuration was the Rochester mechanical fuel-injected 283, which produced 290 horsepower but cost $484.
This 1958 Chevrolet Impala has a 283 under the hood. It has already been rebuilt, and the seller claims only 2,000 miles have been added since the work on the engine was finalized.
There are lots of new parts on this Impala, including a new clutch, a carburetor kit, new hoses and belts, a new radiator, a new fuel tank, and so on. The engine is paired with the 3-speed transmission, also original.
The mechanical part of the car is in perfect shape, so you should be able to drive it without spending a single cent.
The interior was restored to the original settings, but I would still inspect it in person to figure out how original it continues to be - and, to be honest, to determine if the work was indeed a professional restoration.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The interior was replaced with original materials, according to the seller, and the objective was to redo the upholstery to the original specifications.
The Impala continues to be approximately 95% original, according to the seller.
It still wears the original paint and has power steering, power brakes, and electric wipers. It checks many boxes for a collectible, and the only part that requires some attention is the metal. There’s surface rust on the underside, so raise the vehicle on a lift if you are interested in the car, because this is the only way to determine what kind of repairs it needs.
If the damage is only on the surface, dealing with these problems shouldn’t cause any particular challenges, especially if you have a good mechanic.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 I don’t think this is a huge surprise, but this Impala isn’t affordable by any means. Sure, it’s not super-expensive either, and the lack of a 348 combined with that 5% that is no longer original on the car means it must be cheaper than many other siblings out there.
The seller believes $49,000 is a fair price, but if you fire up the eBay listing, you’ll discover that the Make Offer option has also been enabled. This means that you might be able to get a better deal if you are committed to a purchase, but the best way to discuss such details is during a live verification.
You can find the car parked in Canon City, Colorado, and if you live in the same state, driving the car home on its wheels could be a fantastic way to avoid the shipping costs and enjoy the time you spend behind the wheel of a 95% original Chevrolet classic. A clean title is also available, but there’s no mention of any other paperwork.

Musk Is Willing To Crash Tesla Into the Ground so That SpaceX Could Pick Up the Pieces at a Bargain
8 photos
Photo: Tesla
Elon Musk hasn't made a secret of the fact that he wants to fold Tesla into SpaceX. After Musk said committees have been meeting to discuss merger plans, things appear to have advanced to the point that an official announcement is imminent. According to a new report, Elon Musk's two companies will sign the biggest-ever deal as soon as December.
Everyone who has followed Tesla since the early days knows that it's no ordinary company, and Elon Musk is no ordinary CEO. However, the past two years have been a rollercoaster ride. Starting in 2023, Musk has changed Tesla's course, with visible effects into 2024.
At first, it was the cancellation of the Mexico gigafactory, supposedly to speed up the development of Tesla's next-generation EVs and the unboxed manufacturing process. Then, in 2024, Musk appeared to have lost his mind, firing entire teams to cull the workforce in preparation for a market crash that is yet to come. Then he went full MAGA in 2025, jeopardizing Tesla's fate for a future that has now been proven a mistake.
Musk hates that he lost control of Tesla The start of 2026 opened a new window into Musk's vision, or lack thereof. In January, during the Q4 2025 earnings call, Tesla's CEO announced the demise of the Model S/X program, while also revealing that Tesla invested $2 billion in xAI, despite a shareholder vote rejecting the proposal. Musk also announced a $20 billion investment plan, with none of this money going to the automotive sector.
It was the first sign that the controversial CEO had indeed given up on Tesla being a carmaker. Instead, the investments were earmarked for developing new projects in robotics and AI, including data centers. Soon after that, reports indicated that Musk was seriously considering the idea of merging his companies under one big umbrella that he controls.
Not later than February, SpaceX already swallowed the money-losing xAI. If you don't remember, Musk funded xAI as a side project and began diverting resources from Tesla, including GPUs destined for Tesla's data centers. He also used xAI to buy Twitter, thus moving the loss from one company to another. Well, SpaceX investors don't seem to mind, considering that I've heard no complaints about paying for xAI.
Photo: Tesla However, Musk has his eyes on a much bigger prize: he wants Tesla, no less. xAI may have been a diversion to solve some immediate problem, but Tesla was the crown jewel. The truth is, Musk absolutely hates that he no longer has enough Tesla shares to control the company. He sold many of his Tesla shares to buy Twitter as a way to control the narrative prior to the 2024 elections.
A Tesla-SpaceX merger effectively brings Tesla under Musk's control That's why Musk fought tooth and nail for a massive compensation package, even taking Tesla out of Delaware and incorporating it into Texas to secure the bonus. Musk was afraid that his diminished stake in Tesla would make him easy to remove from the company. Indeed, Musk controls about 20% of Tesla, and prospects of gaining more shares are entirely tied to the compensation packages that are yet to come into effect.
However, Musk controls about 85% of SpaceX, and he's not willing to make the same mistake he made with Tesla to dilute his stake. He doesn't want less control; he wants more. That's the idea behind this mega-merger between SpaceX and Tesla. Basically, Musk wants SpaceX, which he controls, to incorporate Tesla, which he doesn't. When the two entities merge, Musk effectively becomes the ruler of Tesla, or whatever remains of it.
Even though Musk never put it that way, it was clear from February that he was essentially preparing a hostile takeover of Tesla by his (then) private company SpaceX. Everything he's done since then appears to converge toward achieving this goal. And it was obvious from the beginning that the less Tesla is valued, the more control Musk has over it after a merger with SpaceX.
For the best merger, Tesla must lose, and SpaceX must gain value Musk has already prepared for this step by increasing the valuation of the money-losing xAI in preparation for the merger with SpaceX. As a result, the February merger artificially increased SpaceX's valuation. Given the outsized stake that Musk owned in both SpaceX and xAI, the merger also strengthened Musk's position before taking over Tesla.
Photo: Tesla That's half the work, though, and the other half is undermining Tesla's position and causing its shares to drop. An undervalued Tesla is a boon for SpaceX and, indeed, Musk, when the SpaceX-Tesla merger completes. And, again, Musk appears to deliver on this front by undermining Tesla's automotive business.
After scrapping the Model S and Model X, the Cybertruck was a natural victim. Officially, all of them had to go because they sold poorly and Tesla had bigger projects to devote to. The Optimus robot line was supposed to replace the Model S/X production line, while the Cybertruck was killed to make way for more Cybercabs. Except neither Optimus nor the Cybercab requires more production capacity. The former doesn't exist, and the latter is already littering parking lots because there's not much use for it.
The most egregious part is not that the slow-selling vehicles have been discontinued, but that Tesla has no plans to build new car models. The Cybertruck platform could've been used for a three-row SUV that everyone wanted. However, Musk has different plans, and a successful Tesla would've interfered with them.
A Tesla-SpaceX merger is no longer hypothetical; it's official Back in January, Bloomberg reported that Musk had already set up two entities in Nevada with the phrase "merger sub" in their names. Both list SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen as an officer, confirming that SpaceX would get an outsized role in this merger. During the SpaceX third-quarter earnings call in October, Musk confirmed that special committees from Tesla and SpaceX are already at work to draw up a merger plan.
Photo: Tesla Now, Bloomberg comes with fresh details about these plans, which appear to have advanced significantly. As I wrote in October, Tesla annual shareholder meeting on December 3 looks like the perfect opportunity to announce the merger plans to shareholders. This should allow Tesla to hold a vote on the merger in early 2027.
According to Bloomberg, Tesla and SpaceX teams have been drawing up the terms of the tie-up and the governance structure of the combined entity, among other matters. If successful, the merger would be the biggest-ever merger deal, potentially creating a $3.5 trillion company. That would put it in the top 5 most valuable companies, ahead of Amazon and in spitting distance of Google.
However, it's not going to be easy to sell this deal to Tesla shareholders, and it's likely that SpaceX will have to pay a premium to convince them. Even if the deal is successful, the resulting entity will have to reconcile national security sensitivities around SpaceX's US defense contracts and Tesla's profitable China manufacturing operations. Musk has dismissed rumors about a spin-off of Tesla's Chinese operations, but this might be inevitable.

This 1958 Chevrolet Yeoman Is No Longer Original, You'll Certainly Like the Upgrades
60 photos
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota
Yeoman is a nameplate that few people remember, and that’s precisely why this specimen is here. It’s no longer an original car, but I’m pretty sure that you’ll like the upgrades, beginning with the looks and ending with what is hiding under the hood.
The car is a custom build that is now trying to find a new home, and the dealer in charge of finding a buyer has priced it quite realistically.
However, I don’t expect the car to find a new home fast. It’ll probably take some time until the right buyer sees it, and considering this is a wagon, it’ll be much harder to appeal to all Chevy fans.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota While the Impala was the model on everybody’s lips in 1958, the full-size Chevrolet lineup as a whole was the one that brought home the bacon that year. Sure, the Impala and the Bel Air accounted for the lion’s share in terms of sales and were the main two models that helped Chevrolet re-secure the leading spot, but the 1958 portfolio included many other choices.
The Yeoman was a wagon based on the Delray . It could be had in two configurations, with two doors and four doors, but in both cases, it offered enough room for six passengers.
The Yeoman didn’t survive for long in Chevrolet’s lineup, as it was discontinued after the 1958 model year. It was offered with the same engine choices as the rest of the full-size Chevys launched that year, beginning with the base 235 six-cylinder Blue Flame engine.
The V8 offering included the base 283 and the big-block 348. For transmissions, customers could choose between a 3-speed close-ratio manual, a 3-speed Overdrive, and a 2-speed Powerglide.
The Yeoman was never a successful model, and depending on who you ask, the production numbers don’t surpass 17K units sold in 1958. Chevrolet ended the year with over 187K wagons sold, so the company didn’t see any reason to retain the Yeoman after this model year.
The Brookwood was the model picked to continue the Yeoman strategy, getting a 2-door wagon version to become the most affordable station wagon you could get in 1959.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota If you missed your chance to get a Yeoman back in the day, finding one today is much more difficult, especially if your target is an original and unmolested specimen.
This specimen has received obvious upgrades, beginning with the two-tone paint, the custom wheels, the tinted glass, and the lowered suspension.
The aggressive stance is completed by new chrome.
Open the door, and you’ll discover a completely new cabin that includes custom black leather seats, updated gauges, LED interior lighting, and a 1,000-watt sound system. There’s a good chance that the cabin feels a lot more comfortable than on the original model, but that wasn’t the purpose of the Yeoman in the first place.
It was an affordable wagon that got the work done, so this particular specimen has been transformed into a completely new car whose purpose is rather to turn heads.
The mechanical part has also received massive upgrades, beginning with the 5.7-liter engine paired with an automatic transmission. You’ll also get a plethora of upgrades, including power steering, power brakes, tuned-port fuel injection, ceramic-coated headers, a dual-exhaust system, a polished aluminum intake, and an aluminum radiator.
I don’t know about you, but this Yeoman looks impressive, especially considering the upgrades under the hood. I don’t think the photos do enough justice to this custom wagon, so my recommendation is that you call the dealer and arrange an in-person inspection. You might be fascinated by how good it looks, so I would start with a walkaround video before discussing how to see the Yeoman live.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota As for the price, this is where things are getting tricky.
This wagon started its life in 1958 as a vehicle supposed to be as affordable as possible. Not everybody wanted to pay a premium for the Impala or the Bel Air, as some buyers only wanted a roomy wagon for typical work around the house or work. The Yeoman was a good choice for two reasons. It sported the same powerful engine as its more expensive brothers, so you could even fit it with a 348.
And second, it was significantly more affordable.
That’s no longer the case today for our specimen, as the upgrades that I mentioned earlier turned it into a rather expensive custom build. The dealer wants $57,000 to let it go, but it also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, just in case you’re looking into a potential purchase but have another deal in mind.
The vehicle is parked in Sarasota, Florida, and considering the listing expires in only a few days, you are running out of time to call the dealer and discuss your options for a live verification and the obvious negotiations regarding the price.

Photo: Screenshot Youtube | AutoYa
With the unveiling of the new-generation X5 behind it, BMW can now focus on expanding the lineup, and one version that has yet to break cover is the upcoming X5 M.
The model offers little to no surprise, because everyone and their neighbor knows that it will sit at the top of the family, being the most agile and punchy version of the premium mid-size crossover, as well as the most expensive. However, we will likely have to wait until 2028 to see it in an official environment, with no camouflage wrapped around its body, as that is when the official unveiling might take place, with an obvious emphasis on the word “might.”
Meanwhile, we will get to see more testers doing their thing in the open, and the rendering world trying to uncover it. Speaking of the latter, it is the reason for this story, as the all-new BMW X5 M that you see above in the gallery is nothing more than a virtual project. Signed by AutoYa and shared on YouTube earlier this week, it offers a preview of the upcoming model, imagining it from a few different angles, while also putting the spotlight on the interior design.
A side-by-side comparison with the regular X5 reveals that the rendered new-gen BMW X5 M features a traditional kidney grille that does not look bad at all. Well, at least not when seeing it next to the grille of the normal X5. It stretches from one headlight to the other, and occupies a much larger chunk of the bumper. The latter has a pair of large air intakes in the middle, a more pronounced integrated splitter, and a pair of redesigned vents on the sides.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | AutoYa The headlights have been tweaked in these digital illustrations, though for the most part, they are almost the same. This also applies to the reflectors on the sides of the front bumper. The hood soldiers on from the regular X5 , and so do the front fenders. The side skirts, on the other hand, are a bit sportier, and the door mirror casings are also new, adopting the typical M design seen on other super sports models from the Munich-based auto marque.
The back end is not entirely visible in these renderings, but we can expect the all-new BMW X5 M to feature the same taillights and tailgate. By the way, the latter component has lost its split-opening design in case you forgot. The bumper and diffuser will, however, be exclusive to the X5 M, as they will contribute to the sportier look. The same goes for the quad tailpipes, as well as the trim on the front fenders, and the wheels, which will further differentiate the regular X5s from the future X5 M.
As mentioned above, the pixel artist has gone as far as imagining the interior of the 2028 BMW X5 M , which features a more traditional-looking steering wheel, exclusive upholstery and trim, dedicated load menus and submenus for the main screens, and a few other things. The cockpit has been rendered in several different colors, and the same goes for the car’s exterior, so picking your favorite should be a walk in the park, assuming you are into the upcoming X5 M, that is.
For what it’s worth, I do not dig the design inside and out, and this comes from someone who believes that the previous generations of the BMW X5 (and X5 M) were some of the prettiest crossovers in the premium mid-size class.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | AutoYa One well-preserved secret when it comes to the next-generation BMW X5 M revolves around the powertrain, and its output and thrust. That’s because we do not know how punchy this model will be. Nevertheless, reports indicate that it should share its plug-in hybrid V8 with the latest M5 and the upcoming one, because the business super sedan is now in line for a Neue Klasse makeover inside and out for the mid-cycle refresh.
The assembly is a plug-in hybrid 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8, which develops 717 hp (727 ps.535 kW) combined on the current BMW M5 and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque. The M5 Sedan and M5 Touring need 3.4 and 3.5 seconds, respectively, to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill. Chances are the upcoming X5 M will be a bit punchier, because it does need to beat its predecessor, which took 3.6 seconds to reach 60 mph.
But then again, the latest BMW M5 is slower than the old one, in case you forgot, so it wouldn’t be a major surprise if the upcoming X5 M ends up being slower than its predecessor.
As previous mentioned, the all-new BMW X5 M might come out sometime in 2028, and it might launch for the 2028 model year in the States, though some believe that it could be a 2029 model by the time it reaches dealers nationwide.

A tanker struck a docked passenger riverboat on the Mississippi River on Friday, triggering a multiagency rescue operation and closing a stretch of the river to vessel traffic.
The 25-foot bitumen tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck American Cruise Lines’ paddlewheel riverboat American Heritage at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time near 1350 Port of New Orleans Place, according to port officials. About 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, were aboard the riverboat, which had docked roughly two hours earlier to begin disembarkation, local media reported.
New Orleans local NBC affiliate WDSU has obtained video showing the initial impact between the tanker Atlantic Asphalt and riverboat American Heritage earlier today. The riverboat had 129 people on board who were in the process of disembarking when it was hit. pic.twitter.com/UuOXcXfGSc — Denn Dunham (@DennD68) November 13, 2026
Video from WDSU showed the larger tanker striking the stationary riverboat, tipping it onto its side and partially submerging it. Footage showed people wearing life jackets in the water near the collision site.
“Multiple individuals have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing,” a New Orleans city spokesperson said. Authorities had not confirmed the number of injuries or the cause of the collision in the initial reports.
BREAKING: A tanker has slammed into a docked river cruise ship on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, with about 129 passengers aboard. CBS News reported at least 14 people were rescued from the water.
The 2017-built tanker is owned by Nave Shipping SA of Liberia and registered in the Marshall Islands.
American Cruise Lines said its passengers and crew had been evacuated and that it was working with emergency authorities. It was not immediately clear whether everyone aboard had been accounted for, NBC News reported.
“We are in close coordination with the U.S. Coast Guard and local authorities,” the company said. “Guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned for everyone involved.”
Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans fire and police departments, the Coast Guard and emergency medical personnel responded. Officials established a triage area inside the Port of New Orleans Administration Building.
The Coast Guard closed the Mississippi River to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 while responders assessed the situation and conducted emergency operations. Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry, who has been serving as a special envoy to Greenland, said he was heading to New Orleans and was in contact with local officials and law enforcement.
“Our immediate priority is the safety of all passengers, crew members and first responders,” the Port of New Orleans said in a statement. “This remains an active and evolving incident.”
Why it matters: The collision created an immediate threat to passengers and crew aboard a docked vessel while also halting vessel movements along one of the busiest stretches of the Mississippi River.

NASCAR Driver Joey Logano Drives His Super Truck for the First Time: It's a Raptor R With a Twist
11 photos
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube
NASCAR driver Joey Logano has just taken delivery of his VelociRaptoR. It is, in fact, a Ford F-150 Raptor R with a twist. It is a 1,000-horsepower twist signed by Hennessey Performance and transformed into the ultimate high-performance off-road truck.
NASCAR drivers don't drive Mitsubishi Mirages or Toyota Priuses. It is in their bllood to go for the most powerful and fastest vehicles out there. When the standard car market is not enough, they raise the stakes. This is what three-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Joey Logano did.
Even if he is used to taming hundreds of horsepower at the track, he was so pumped up on delivery day that he got up at 4 A.M. Company founder John Hennessey personally traveled to North Carolina to hand over the new owner of the super truck at his own dealership, Huntersville Ford, in November 2026.
The dealership is located near his home and his production studio in the Charlotte metro area and specializes in lifted trucks, supercharged builds, and performance models through an on-site custom accessory shop and its "Logano Speed Works" builds. Now, his truck will tower over all those sitting in the parking lot of his dealership, which opened in May 2026.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube The monstrous VelociRaptoR is basically a Ford F-150 Raptor R with a twist. It’s been touched by Hennessey Performance’s magic wand, which transformed it into the most powerful pickup truck with a combustion engine out there.
The F-150 Raptor R rolls off the production line of Ford’s Dearborn Truck Plant in Michigan with a 5.2-liter supercharged V8 under the hood. The V8, derived from the GT500’s Predator, pumps out 720 horsepower (730 metric horsepower) and 640 pound-feet (868 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what makes it flash from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.6 seconds, run the quarter mile in 12.0 seconds with a trap speed of 112 mph (180 kph), and max out at a top speed of 114 mph (183 kph), electronically limited due to the speed rating of its massive 37-inch off-road tires.
However, those numbers are no longer valid because Hennessey Performance upgraded the factory V8 to produce a massive 1,000 horsepower and 1,000 pound-feet of torque (with the help of a new 3.8-liter supercharger mounted on top of the engine. However, from the passenger seat, John Hennessey tells him the actual number is 1,200 horsepower (1,217 metric horsepower).
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube The 6,500-pound (2,948-kilogram) monster got upgraded wheels and tires, while six-piston Brembo brakes handle the extra oomph, because at 1,000 horsepower (1,014 metric horsepower) and 1,000 pound-feet (1,356 Newton meters) of torque, you need all the grip and brake power that you can get.
Now, the Ford F-150 Raptor R-based truck has shaved off half a second of the 0-to-60 time, being clocked at 3.1 seconds, and takes 11.4 seconds to run the quarter mile, but the speed limit hasn't changed due to the limitation of those off-road tires.
Joey Logano's VelociRaptoR wears a custom front bumper, which integrates LED off-road lights. The truck also got a custom cabin, trimmed in leather and Alcantara with contrasting orange accents all throughout. The build also got an upgraded serial plaque under the hood and a hidden Easter egg, featuring its owner’s personal racing logo.
Now, the world-class race car driver Joey Logano, with no fewer than 39 wins under his belt, takes his brand-new truck for a spin to see what he can do. In his hands, it pulls like a freight train, but the traction control is a little overwhelmed by his quick reactions.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube Joye’s brand-new VelociRaptoR will join an exclusive collection of cars. In his garage, he has the most powerful production Ford Mustang ever built, the GTD with its 815 horsepower (826 metric horsepower), a 2017 Ford GT Heritage Edition, a 1971 Ford Mustang Mach, a 1980 Ford Mustang Fox Body, and a Ford Model A Rat Rod and a Model T among his Blue Oval-badged cars, because the man has raced with Ford his whole life.
His garage also hosts a DeLorean DMC-12 , a 1972 Oldsmobile Cutlass, and a 1993 Ferrari 512 TR. His retired NASCAR Cup Series trophy cars are also there, but because they are not street legal, these are the only ones that he doesn’t drive and only keeps as display pieces.
In the meantime, Joey Logano drove the Number 22 Team Penske Ford Mustang Dark Horse in the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. Ford also unveiled the updated Mustang Dark Horse S body style that he will race next season.
While the street-legal Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC makes 795. Horsepower (806 metric horsepower), Joey Logano’s NASCAR Cup Series race version is regulated to produce 670 or 750 horsepower, depending on the track. That is far under what his brand-new VelociRaptoR can do.

West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey said major state electric utility Appalachian Power will invest $17 billion to build new natural gas-fired power plants in the state. The Republican governor on November 12 also announced that the generator is making a separate $7.5-billion commitment to upgrade existing coal-fired power plants in the state.
“West Virginia has some of the greatest energy resources in the country, and our people should benefit from them,” said Morrisey on Thursday. “Families are struggling with rising costs, and too many are seeing more of their paychecks consumed by electric bills. We’re tackling that problem from both directions, helping families reduce their energy use while increasing the supply of affordable, reliable electricity.”
Said Morrisey, “Power bills will not go up; they must not go up because of these new additions. And we’ve been assured that they will not. And I will look to enforce that any way I can.”
Appalachian Power’s $17-billion investment is expected to add about 3 GW of gas-fired generation capacity by 2031. Officials said building new power plants will create more than 2,000 jobs during construction, along with about 100 permanent positions at the facilities. Morrisey in a video announcement of the investments said there are three plans for new power plant projects that will be “geographically dispersed” across the state. He said the locations of the facilities, along with other details, would be announced later.
Major Commitment for New Generation
Thursday’s announcement is considered the largest commitment for the addition of new power generation capacity in the state since the early 1970s, when plans were unveiled for the 2.9-GW John Amos Power Plant. The coal-fired Amos plant, the largest power station in American Electric Power’s fleet, entered service from 1971-1973, and is expected to continue operating at least through 2040.
Appalachian Power said its $7.5-billion commitment is for upgrades to coal-fired power plants between now and 2050. The company owns three coal-fired power stations in West Virginia: John Amos in Winfield, the 1.3-GW Mountaineer in New Haven, and the 1.6-GW Mitchell in Moundsville.
The governor’s office has said the work announced Thursday is related to Morrisey’s ratepayer protection pledge, which is meant to ensure that costs for new power generation infrastructure in West Virginia are not passed on to residential and business electricity customers. Officials have said that electricity prices will not rise due to the work.
Morrisey, who took office in January 2025, launched his “50 by 50” initiative in September of that year. The program, which aims to triple the amount of power generation capacity in the state, from about 16 GW to 50 GW, to date has announced an additional 11.67 GW of capacity—about one-third of the amount needed to hit the 50-GW target. The $17-billion investment announced Thursday brings total private-sector investment in West Virginia to $113.6 billion in the past year, according to the governor’s office.
“While other states are restricting energy production and retiring reliable power plants, West Virginia is increasing its energy supply,” said Morrisey. “By protecting our existing generation and building the capacity we’ll need for decades to come, we will strengthen reliability, create good-paying jobs, and work toward more affordable electricity for West Virginia families and businesses.”
Google Program
Among those investments is Google’s $10-million Energy Impact Program, which includes an initial $1-million investment through the West Virginia Office of Energy to help families in six of the state’s counties make home repairs necessary to qualify for energy rebates. The money also supports energy efficiency efforts for local governments and nonprofits groups in the state.
Officials said more than 1,400 state residents have applied for Home Energy Rebate programs since their launch just more than one month ago. Other Office of Energy programs are directing funds toward power grid upgrades to improve electricity reliability, along with putting money toward energy efficiency improvements that will benefit nonprofit organizations and local governments.
West Virginia’s generation capacity buildout includes projects such as FirstEnergy subsidiary Mon Power’s proposed 1.2-GW combined-cycle natural gas-fired plant at the Fort Martin station near Maidsville in Monongalia County. That facility, with an estimated cost of $2.5 billion, is projected to open in late 2031.
Competitive Power Venture’s Shay Energy Center in Doddridge County, a planned 2.1-GW combined-cycle natural gas-fired plant, is scheduled to start construction next year. In addition, Mon Power and Potomac Edison have advanced smaller solar generation installations that include about 70 MW of generation capacity across Preston, Hancock, and Tucker counties.
Kindle Energy earlier this year broke ground for the Wolf Summit Energy project, a 600-MW combined-cycle gas-fired station in Harrison County. That project is supported by Blackstone and will serve customers of Old Dominion Electric Cooperative.
— Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

Cargo thieves stole more than $150 million in artificial intelligence equipment between June 2025 and June 2026, increasingly using fraudulent carrier identities and falsified shipping documents to steal high-value shipments, according to a report from Overhaul.
The company’s AI Infrastructure Intel Report, released Oct. 21, analyzed 111 different AI equipment theft incidents across the United States from 2023 through June 2026. The number of incidents increased 34% since 2024, according to Overhaul.
The report comes weeks after the recent theft of $11.4 million in NVIDIA hardware from a shipment traveling from Oakland, California, to Fort Worth, Texas. Oakland police said the theft was reported Sept. 13 and remains under investigation, with no arrests announced.
Overhaul’s $150 million estimate covers a 12-month period from June 2025 through June 2026. By comparison, Scott Cornell, chair of TAPA Americas and an executive at SPG Cargo & Logistics, estimated that $110.6 million in data center freight had been stolen between June 3 and Aug. 14, 2026, when he shared the figure during an appearance on FreightWaves’ Fraud Watch podcast . The estimates cover different periods and categories of freight. Cornell’s estimate also predates the $11.4 million NVIDIA shipment theft, which was picked up on Aug. 29.
In the report, fraud or deception was involved in 92% of the reported thefts. Overhaul described incidents as deceptive pickups when criminals use tactics such as identity theft, fraudulent carrier identities and altered bills of lading to obtain shipments.
The report includes incidents identified within Overhaul’s own network, as well as thefts reported across the industry through open and closed intelligence sources. Overhaul sells supply chain visibility and risk management services.
The sheer value of AI equipment makes it an attractive target for cargo thieves . Overhaul estimates a single flagship AI server rack costs roughly $3 million, meaning a truckload of computing hardware can represent millions of dollars in potential losses.
“As thieves become increasingly deceptive, visibility into a shipment alone isn’t enough to stop it from being taken,” Barry Conlon, CEO and founder of Overhaul, said in the release. The report’s conclusion that visibility alone is not enough supports the case for Overhaul’s broader services.
The increase in AI equipment theft comes amid a broader rise in cargo crime across North America. Verisk CargoNet recorded 2,646 confirmed thefts in the United States and Canada in 2025, an 18% increase from the previous year. Estimated losses reached nearly $725 million, up 60%, while the average value per theft climbed to $273,990.
The financial impact of AI equipment theft can extend beyond the value of the stolen cargo. Overhaul estimates that for every dollar of stolen hardware covered by an insurance claim, roughly $3 in additional losses go unclaimed. The company said the 3:1 ratio is a conservative estimate based on a RAND research paper . Those indirect costs include deployment delays, lost contract eligibility, regulatory and compliance exposure, and additional security investments.
The incidents highlight a challenge for shippers and logistics providers moving high-value technology: Tracking a shipment’s location may not be enough when criminals can impersonate legitimate carriers and manipulate shipping documents. Verifying the identity of the person collecting a load and confirming that they are authorized to transport it are also critical to preventing theft.
Why this matters
The growing value of AI infrastructure is creating new opportunities for cargo thieves, who are increasingly using carrier impersonation and fraudulent paperwork to intercept shipments. For shippers and logistics providers, tracking technology alone may not be enough to prevent losses as verifying carrier identities and pickup authorization becomes increasingly important. Overhaul provides supply chain visibility, risk management and cargo security solutions designed to help companies monitor shipments and prevent theft.

New York State has come out on top in a legal battle with the Department of Transportation over how long a non-domiciled CDL can stay in effect.
In a unanimous decision issued Friday by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, a three-judge panel agreed with New York’s argument that denial of a portion of the state’s federal transportation funds over the issue of non-domiciled CDL eligibility was “arbitrary and capricious.”
The federal DOT in April said it was denying New York State approximately 4% of its normal funding after it objected to New York’s policies on non-domiciled CDLs.
Specifically, the federal government including the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA)–which was a defendant in the case brought by New York –said New York was granting non domiciled CDLs to non-citizens whose authorization to stay in the U.S. expired before the amount of time on the license, which could be as much as eight years.
New York’s counter argument was that there is nothing in federal law that requires a non-domiciled CDL to end prior to the expiration of a driver’s authorized stay in the U.S.
Lots of money at stake
The amount impacted by the DOT’s ruling: $73,502,543.
The panel was unambiguous in rejecting FMCSA’s argument that federal rules allowed denial of funds over the mismatch between expiration of a CDL and a person’s legal ability to stay in the country.
“As FMCSA itself concedes, the plain text of the federal regulations in place during the relevant period did not contain an expiration-matching requirement,” the judges wrote in their rejection of the federal government’s arguments. “The regulatory structure and history confirm that conclusion.”
To obtain a CDL, beyond the normal requirements of meeting the operational tests, non-domiciled CDL holders needed to present “lawful presence documentation instead of proof of citizenship or lawful permanent residency,” the judges said in summarizing the history of the dispute. The CDL could only have a term of “five years after initial issuance and eight years after renewal—the same as for domiciled licenses,” the court wrote.
That documentation could be an unexpired Employment Authorization Document (EAD) or a foreign passport along with an approved I-94 form. The I-94 is given to foreign visitors when they arrive legally in the U.S.
More than 30k potentially affected
The size of the universe in question is not small, according to the judges’ summary: about 32,600 non-domiciled CDLs or Commercial Learning Permit holders in New York, which it said was about 7% of the licenses in the state.
(New York is not the only state where this battle is ongoing. There is a similar suit before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia between the federal government and California).
After a review of the state’s practices in 2025, FMCSA found that “New York was substantially noncompliant with federal regulations,” the court said in its summary. Its objections were the CDLs that ran past a license holder’s expiration date for being in the U.S.
New York said that “requirement” wasn’t in the law and that it couldn’t be in violation of a rule that didn’t exist.
But as the court said in its summary, “FMCSA stated that the expiration matching requirement was ‘not a new requirement,’ and that its ‘focus on other aspects of a State’s CDL program in previous years’ did not preclude it from enforcing the requirement now.”
In backing New York, the court said FMCSA had “conceded in its final determination, throughout its appellate briefing and at oral argument that the plain text of the regulation does not contain a matching requirement.”
The ‘common sense’ defense
But the agency also argued against a “literal” reading of the regulation, the court said. FMCSA argued that its interpretation of the regulations was “common sense,” the court wrote.
“FMCSA’s concession that a ‘literal’ reading of the ‘clear’ words of its own regulations supports New York’s understanding should be the end of the matter,” the court wrote.
But asking New York to “infer” that what FMCSA’s actions were the intent of the law “is unsupported by the regulatory text,” according to the court.
“All in all, the regulatory history reflects that, before September 2025, states were not required to tailor non-domiciled CDL validity periods to the expiration dates on lawful presence paperwork,” the court wrote in its summary. The court said the 2011 rule that FMCSA was enforcing doesn’t contain such a matching requirement, and noted that FMCSA had decided “not to enforce an expiration-matching requirement until now.”
“FMCSA has not pointed to a single instance before the final determination in this case when it found a state noncompliant for failing to adhere to that requirement,” the judges wrote.

Massive Buick Encasa Minivan Has 713 Imaginary HP and Rocks the World of North American CGI MPVs
23 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
If you want the latest news about General Motors in relation to its Buick brand, the marque has a sleek new hybrid sedan dubbed Buick Electra GS with two plug-in hybrid powertrains, but it’s not for North America.
Instead, at home, General Motors is reportedly planning to spend no less than $750 million to electrify the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia with hybrid versions , according to Reuters. All three SUVs with three rows are produced at GM’s Lansing Delta Township plant in Michigan, and the company has so far acknowledged it has plans to retool the factory for hybrid production, without actually revealing the HEV models it plans.
The decision could impact a lot of customers: a variety of buyers are growing more concerned about fuel costs, so it’s logical that GM is looking to broaden its powertrain lineup after previously investing heavily in EVs that are out of favor in the US while leaving hybrids to popular brands from Asia or Europe. Better late than never, of course, so that course of action got people thinking – including the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, apparently.
For example, Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Buick minivan to add to the new and upcoming hybrid roster from GM. In his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project, we find a cool headline: “Buick is building a 713-hp minivan that makes the GNX look slow.”
Of course, he doesn’t want a fight with his followers, and thus he further explains: “I mean a high horsepower van would be awesome stateside, but I guess the cool Buicks are only for Asia now. And nothing makes the GNX look slow.” So, he took the Chinese Buick Electra Encasa minivan introduced at the 2025 Guangzhou Auto Show and adapted it with the attitude of an American land yacht and a proposed 713-hp powertrain, most likely of the PHEV variety rather than a full EV.
While this project is merely wishful thinking, a Buick minivan isn’t a bad idea per se. The US automaker has become a crossover SUV -only brand in America with the Envista, Encore GX, Envision, and Enclave on sale. A Buick Encasa would fit right in with the moniker series, and maybe it’s not a bad idea to compete with the Chrysler Pacifica, Toyota Sienna, Honda Odyssey, and the Kia Carnival across the US minivan sector, which is experiencing a return to form as of late.
So, what do you think? Would you buy something like this or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)

All-New NX5 Hyundai Tucson Gets the Blacked-Out Treatment Along With Two New Alloy Wheels - in CGI
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Asian automakers like Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Subaru, or Mazda have supported subtle yet stable growth across the US automotive market in October, with deliveries slowly rebounding from the shocks of all the geopolitical unrest, and it's mainly because folks are now flocking to hybrids.
American Honda achieved its best October over the past six years; Hyundai announced its best-ever October with 73,452 units and a 5% increase compared to last year, plus a ten-month performance up by three percent to 770,916 units; Kia followed swiftly with +16% to 80k units and a ten-month total of 747k units, while Subaru soared by 6% in October and Mazda jumped by no less than 25% during the same month!
Quite obviously, the brands that have popular models attracted even more attention due to their good mix of gasoline, hybrid, and PHEV models. Hyundai, in particular, experienced a massive push for the Santa Fe, Kona, Ioniq 5, Elantra, and Palisade. The Tucson also remained on top with almost 200k units and a 6% increase so far this year!
And that’s only the beginning, since the South Korean automaker announced the upcoming all-new fifth-generation Hyundai Tucson back in August at home in South Korea, then presented it in front of the Old Continent’s crowds during the recent 2026 Paris Motor Show. Hyundai’s new Tucson looks dramatically changed compared to the current one and has a tech-savvy cabin with fewer buttons, making it a major departure from the model it replaces.
According to reports from at home in Korea, it immediately broke the one-day pre-order record when the order books opened for the new iteration. But the radical redesign featuring the Art of Steel design language and the new Pleos infotainment system remains a mystery for North America. Hopefully, the automaker won’t be late to the party and could introduce it to the local audience during the upcoming 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show taking place November 20-29 at the Los Angeles Convention Center.
Until then, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI for a moment to showcase their vision for a cool North American introduction from across Imagination Land: Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, says his perfect new Hyundai Tucson is blacked-out and has two types of new aftermarket-style wheels: one looking like aero covers and another with a fancy multi-spoke design.
The differences compared to the regular NX5 Hyundai Tucson are pretty easy to spot because the pixel master also created a ‘before and after’ collage, showing the Hyundai Tucson ‘ Black ’ with absolutely no other touches of color aside from the dark hue that was Henry Ford’s favorite not long ago.
